lesson: [lfm2.5_2.6b] Clusters picked from the output side barely mattered. 64 w2 columns with the strongest logit-lens alignment to a skill's category words (L23 ordinal cosine .14 vs a .067 baseline; colour and weekday writers) dropped their skill by only .02-.06. Whole-MLP ablation, attribution seeds and gate-span growth found the real parts.

[lfm2.5_2.6b] Gate-span growth turned small attribution seeds into large passing MLP clusters. Take about 8 attribution seeds, add every unit whose w1 row projects onto the seeds' gate-row span, and subtract 2-4x the projection onto seed spans of skills that leak. Passes: L23 facts, 1024 units, −.44 (random ≤ .12); L25 roman, 1024 units, −.39 (random ≤ .02); L12 and L13 month, 2048 units each, −.19 and −.21 with weekday about −.03. Subtracting a 48-64-unit basis taken from an already-screened facts cluster removed facts leaks better than subtracting 8 seeds.

[lfm2.5_2.6b] Ranking heads by static OV (embedding of input word → unembedding of target, compared with the word itself) predicted real head groups. L21 head 20 writes the antonym at z +5.8 and suppresses the word at z −7.5; heads 3, 10, 20, 27 cut antonym −.39 (random ≤ .05). L27 head 28 writes the irregular past form at z +13.3 (31: +6.1, 17: +4.7); heads 17, 28, 30, 31 cut past tense −.28 (random ≤ .04). Head group effects are non-additive, so verify each 4-6-head subset by ablation and swap one head at a time.

[lfm2.5_2.6b] Facts passes beat random only narrowly in L3, L24, L25 and L26 MLPs (random 2048-4096-unit parts dropped facts .25-.34), and L25 passed at essentially chance (.216 vs .214). Month clusters that were clean on the search split (.16-.25) failed the held-out check in L9, L21 and L23. In L5 and L13, random head groups often include critical heads (L5 head 1 drops everything; random L13 groups dropped month up to .76), so screens there fail against random. Prefer L17, L21 and L27 heads.

[lfm2.5_2.6b] Robust skills hid in one key head. capital_city (base .93) never dropped selectively from any MLP cluster, but L21 head 7 plus heads 3, 10, 28 cut it −.73 (random ≤ .04). Math, code and multilingual found no selective unit: math stayed within .12 for every whole MLP tested, and no 1-2-layer block was selective for any skill.

[lfm2.5_2.6b] Seeded weight-similarity families work here, but on this model they need large sizes. The L19 past_tense family came from attribution seeds 6016/5224/7020/1589. Units were ranked by 0.5*cos(w1 row)+0.5*cos(w2 column) to the seeds, minus the max score against month and weekday seeds. Its drop grew with size: 256→.14, 512→.163, 1024→.185, 2048→.248. Only 2048 passed (1024 failed the held-out check). Other skills moved under .04 and random 2048-unit parts at most .022.

[lfm2.5_2.6b] Penalise the families of skills that live in the same layer. Without month seeds (3640/4442/3004/4105) in the penalty, the L19 past-tense family leaked month_successor .057-.074, above the target/3 limit. With the penalty, the month leak fell to .029-.032 and the target drop was unchanged. Run a quick attribution scan of the leaking skill in that layer to get the penalty seeds.

[lfm2.5_2.6b] Weight-only selection on the input side was inert. L3 clusters of 512 units, ranked by w1/w3 rows (after ffn_norm) aligned with category-word embedding directions, dropped weekday .036, past .019 and ordinal .013. Per-layer top-256 alignment scores were noise-level (about .01 against a .001 mean). Use attribution seeds and grow from them instead.

[lfm2.5_2.6b] Head quads chosen from top attribution in the attention layers (2,5,9,13,17,21,24,27) were too broad. L17 [7,8,21,22] cut weekday .257 but also month .49, facts .24 and object_color .15. L13 [1,4,13,22], the top heads for code and multilingual, damaged everything (facts .41, object_color .66, its control .79). Whole block L19 also hit month .31 and weekday .16 while improving past_tense.

[lfm2.5_2.6b] Some seeded families plateau below the threshold however big they get. Object colour at L22 (seed 3374, attribution .047) gave .085/.091/.107 at 256/1024/2048. Month at L19 gave .113/.112 at 1024/2048. Code at L10 (seed 9672) went broad, hitting facts .158 and general_text .173. If the drop at 1024 is under about .12, move to another layer or seed set rather than growing further.
[harness] Handle files are looked up in lowercase. py:NAME resolves to /work/name.json, so save every JSON filename in lowercase or ablate reports that the file does not exist.

[lfm2.5_2.6b] A seed that clearly dominates its skill's attribution grew into clean, large late-layer MLP parts. L26 unit 5781 led object_color with .087, against .046 for the next unit. Units were ranked by 0.25*cos(w1 row) + 0.25*cos(w3 row) + 0.5*cos(w2 column) to the mean of seeds 5781 and 10038, minus the score against a capital_city seed. The 256- and 1024-unit families both passed object_color (.26 and .262), with other skills ≤.048, controls ≤.004 and random draws ≤.02.

[lfm2.5_2.6b] The same seed growth from weak seeds stayed under the bar. L22 object_color seeds (3374 at .047) gave .073 at 256 units and .094 at 1024, where a random 1024-unit part reached .115. L25 capital seed 4209 (.015) gave .047, and the L28 antonym seeds (.014-.018 each) gave .121 with object_color leaking .111. On this model the seed needs about .08 or more attribution to make a passing family.

[lfm2.5_2.6b] Attribution seeds shared across skills produce broad families. L27 unit 5333 ranked top for capital_city and also for object_color and weekday, and its 512-unit family hit facts .12, past_tense .10, month .10 and antonym .08 but capital_city only .085. The L28 antonym seeds were also math's top units, a sign they are generic completion units. Check whether a seed shows up in other skills' top lists before growing it.

[lfm2.5_2.6b] L22 code seed 8153 (.034) reads out as subword fragments like 'Net', 'Bay', '-man'. Its 256-unit family dropped code only .066 but leaked to roman .108 and facts .096. The code built-in has a low base (.31) and looks spread out, so MLP families are poor targets for it in mid layers.

[lfm2.5_2.6b] Picking the top 2048 L22 MLP units by w2 column norm alone was broad, not a skill part: object_color .196, month .16, facts .137 and roman .127 all dropped together. Ranking by norm alone mostly selects general-purpose writers.
